title: Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities
body_text:
Education being a subject of the Concurrent List of the Constitution, both the Centre and States/ UTs are responsible for the Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and Schools in the country.
The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under the Ministry of Education including Central Universities, are statutory autonomous organizations established under respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed by provisions of the  Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations made thereunder. As autonomous institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The recruitment powers vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive  Committee/Board of Management.
State Universities are established through respective State Acts and vacancies therein are filled by concerned State Governments/ Universities themselves. Vacancy details of State Universities are not maintained centrally.
An Institution is declared as Deemed to be University by the Central Government, on the advice of University Grants Commission (UGC), under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. The  Institutions Deemed to be Universities are regulated by the UGC as per the UGC (Institutions  deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. As per these Regulations, the Executive Council of the Institution appoints faculty staff and such other posts on the recommendation of the Selection Committee, in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Minimum  Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and other Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education)  Regulations, 2018.
Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to  promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity  in existing institutions.
In centrally financed Higher Education Institutions, measures have been taken to attract quality faculties which includes year-round open advertisements, recruitment through search-cum selection procedures, special recruitment drive, mission mode recruitment and invitation to  alumni/scientists/faculty, etc. The faculty recruitment processes are carried out by the CHEIs by inviting applications in a transparent manner, as part of a multi-step and robust screening process. The Acts and Statutes of various institutions specify the composition of selection  committees, authorities responsible for recruitment of various levels of faculty, provision of  independent subject experts and visitor’s nominees etc. so as to ensure transparency and academic rigour in recruitments. UGC has launched a common portal ‘CU-CHAYAN’ for  faculty recruitment, making provision for listing of vacancies/ advertisements/ jobs across all Central Universities, thus making the entire recruitment process more transparent and accessible.
The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, lays emphasis on improving the overall quality of education in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) through a set of initiatives that include promotion of multidisciplinary education, nurturing critical thinking and analytical ability, promoting research and innovation, improving the quality of infrastructure, effective and qualitative teacher training etc.
To improve the quality of education, several initiatives have been institutionalised in centrally funded institutions. The Government of India provides financial support to state governments under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)/ Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM USHA) scheme, for improvement in Higher Education. The Government of India has also launched the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP) in 2023 across the country to improve teaching quality, strengthen institutional performance, and promote better academic outcomes in Higher Educational Institutions. The program is implemented through 151 Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centres (MMTTCs). So far, more than 4 lakh faculty members have been trained across the country.
In August, 2021, all CHEIs under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook  special recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled  Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode.  From September 2022, all CHEIs including Central Universities (CUs) have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drives to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of the last  Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757  faculty positions, in Mission Mode.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.
*****
RRTN

enrichment.summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply, the Minister of State for Education informed Parliament about the framework for filling faculty vacancies in Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs), noting that recruitment is done autonomously by respective institutions while state university vacancies are not centrally tracked. The reply detailed Mission Mode recruitment drives since 2021, under which 32,114 posts, including 18,757 faculty positions, have been filled up to 23 May 2026. It also referenced quality initiatives like UGC's CU-CHAYAN portal and the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP).
enrichment.context:
Faculty vacancies in India's higher education institutions, especially reservation backlog vacancies for SC/ST/OBC categories, have been a persistent governance concern affecting teaching quality and social justice objectives in academia. Since education is on the Concurrent List, the Centre's direct control is limited to Central Universities and other CHEIs, while states manage their own universities, leading to fragmented vacancy data nationally. The government's repeated 'Mission Mode' exhortations (2021, 2022, 2025) reflect an ongoing struggle to fill backlog and regular vacancies despite institutional autonomy in recruitment.

This release also ties into the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020's broader push for quality higher education through multidisciplinary learning, research promotion, and better teacher training. Programs like MMTTP (2023) and the CU-CHAYAN portal represent governance tools to standardize and improve transparency in faculty recruitment and training across Central Universities. Schemes like RUSA/PM USHA extend central financial support to states for higher education quality improvement, illustrating the Centre-State partnership model in a concurrent subject area.

prelims_questions.question: Under which section of the UGC Act, 1956, is an institution declared as 'Deemed to be University' by the Central Government?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, institutions are declared 'Deemed to be University' under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, on the advice of the UGC.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding higher education governance in India is correct, based on recent parliamentary information?
options: Education is placed exclusively in the Union List of the Constitution
Vacancy details of State Universities are maintained centrally by the UGC
Faculty recruitment in Central Universities is done by the Ministry of Education directly
Central Higher Education Institutions are autonomous bodies where recruitment powers vest with their Board of Governors/Executive Committee/Board of Management
prelims_questions.explanation: The release clarifies that CHEIs are statutory autonomous organizations where recruitment powers vest with their respective Board of Governors/Executive Committee/Board of Management, and education is on the Concurrent List, not the Union List.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the challenges in filling faculty vacancies in Central Higher Education Institutions in India. Evaluate the effectiveness of 'Mission Mode' recruitment drives and other government initiatives in addressing this issue.

Education being a subject on the Concurrent List creates a fragmented governance structure for Higher Education Institutions. Critically examine the implications of this arrangement for policy coordination, accountability, and quality assurance in Indian higher education.
